The summary is mostly usable but has an unsupported headline figure, redundancy, and a weak example set, so an investigator would need to redo some analysis.","problems":["Headline says '21% of notes describe data review with no test on the claim', but tools show 6 of 29 notes (20.7%), or 6 of 19 moderate-plus notes (31%); the 21% is not clearly defined and could mislead.","The headline's '17% are duplicates' is not explained in the body, which omits the duplicate rate (0.172), so it is not carried through or interpreted.","Rationale repeats itself: the 99215 share vs expected appears twice and bulk-created/paste-heavy appear twice, which adds clutter.","Example claims are both low-complexity 99215s but only two are cited out of 25 available, and none of the high-complexity or documented-supported claims are mentioned, so the evidence is thin.","The 5% comparison rate for below-billed 99215 is not on the card (card gives 4.8% for all providers; 5% is a rounding), and the 0 of 9 result is not tied to the weak signal that most documented 99215s were supported.","The summary says 'notes may be inflated' but the tool output says looks_inflated false, which is a mild inconsistency; it also never flags missing information such as minutes not recorded or the illegible/missing-results deficiencies.","Next steps are generic: no concrete request for the 6 notes with data reviewed but no test, and no mention of the ILLEGIBLE/MISSING_RESULTS deficiencies or of specific patients with repeated 99215 visits."]}
